name: St. Mary of the Angels Basilica
history: The parish began in 1852 with a small wooden "shanty" church paid for with $300 from railroad workers, dedicated to St. Mary of the Angels after the Franciscan mother church at Assisi. The present church was built from 1913 to 1917 for $250,000. Pope Francis named it a basilica on 14 February 2017, the 83rd in the U.S.
arch: Gothic Revival by French-trained architect Emile Ulrich of Cleveland, with twin 150-foot towers and stone steeples, built almost entirely of white marble from nearby Pennsylvania.
features: The altars, railing, pulpit and baptismal font are Carrara marble from Italy.
It stands near the Allegheny River in downtown Olean.

look.d: The whole front is Pennsylvania white marble.

fun: Spiritual writer Thomas Merton came to Olean in 1940 to teach at nearby St. Bonaventure.
journal: Railroad workers' $300 shanty became twin marble steeples.
